name: Serbia
tagline: A confluence capital with the best nightlife in the Balkans, and monasteries frescoed eight hundred years ago.
summary: Serbia sits on the Danube where central Europe stops being central Europe. Belgrade has been destroyed and rebuilt dozens of times and behaves accordingly — unsentimental, loud and very good company. The north, Vojvodina, is flat, Hungarian-influenced and full of paprika; the south and west hold medieval monasteries with frescoes among the finest in Orthodox Europe.

season.note: Late spring and early autumn are best; Belgrade in July is hot and the river barges are the only sensible place to be. Winter is cold and the trumpet festival at Guča in August is a phenomenon in its own right.

getting_around: Buses cover the country densely; the Belgrade–Novi Sad fast railway opened recently. The Šargan Eight narrow-gauge line in the west is a ride for its own sake.
food: Ćevapi and pljeskavica, grilled and enormous
Ajvar, roast red pepper relish, made at home each autumn
Rakija, fruit brandy, offered on arrival and refusing it is difficult

festivals.name: EXIT festival, in a Habsburg fortress

know: Not in the EU; the dinar is the currency and cash is more useful outside cities.
Positions on Kosovo are politically charged here — visitors are best served by listening rather than opining.
Smoking indoors is more common than elsewhere in Europe.

regions.name: Belgrade & Vojvodina
regions.summary: The capital at the meeting of two rivers, and the flat Habsburg north above it.

cities.name: Belgrade
cities.summary: A fortress above the confluence of the Sava and the Danube, with floating clubs below it and brutalist New Belgrade opposite.
highlights: Kalemegdan fortress at sunset over the two rivers
Splavovi — river barges that are bars and clubs, all summer
Skadarlija's bohemian street and the kafanas along it
New Belgrade's socialist modernism, taken seriously by architects

experiences.name: A kafana with live music
experiences.summary: Long tables, a small band moving between them, rakija, and no fixed end time.

cities.name: Novi Sad
cities.summary: A Habsburg river city under the Petrovaradin fortress, with wine hills behind it.
highlights: Petrovaradin's fortress and its 16 km of underground galleries
Fruška Gora: sixteen monasteries in a wooded ridge
Vojvodina's Hungarian and Slovak food villages

regions.name: Western & Southern Serbia
regions.summary: River canyons, a narrow-gauge railway, and the medieval monastery frescoes.

cities.name: Mokra Gora
cities.summary: A mountain village on the Šargan Eight, a narrow-gauge line that climbs a figure of eight to gain height.
highlights: The Šargan Eight, 22 tunnels in 15 kilometres
Drvengrad, a wooden village built as a film set and kept
The Tara national park and the Drina canyon

experiences.name: The Šargan Eight
experiences.summary: A 760 mm gauge line that loops over itself to climb 300 metres; two and a half hours and a great deal of leaning out of windows.

cities.name: Studenica
cities.summary: A 12th-century monastery of white marble in a wooded valley, with frescoes from 1209 and monks still living there.
highlights: The Crucifixion fresco, a landmark of Byzantine painting
White marble churches inside a circular wall
The valley, which has almost nothing else in it
